title: Celigo guardrail
description:
Configuration for a guardrail import. `_connectionId` is only
required for BYOK `ai_agent` guardrails.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Guardrails evaluate structured records only. Do not send the import-level `blob` or
`blobKeyPath` fields — either one fails the save with 422 `not_supported`
("Field "blob" is not supported for this import type").

Do not put a `tools` array anywhere under `guardrail.aiAgent` — a non-empty array on
any provider block fails the save with 422 `guardrail_tools_not_allowed`.

description.description: Optional description of the guardrail's purpose.
examples: Scans records for PII and masks detected values before import.

_connectionId.description:
Connection for BYOK (bring your own key) — only meaningful for `ai_agent` type
guardrails. Optional for the built-in providers (`openai`, `gemini`, `anthropic`),
which run on platform-managed credentials when it is omitted; catalog providers
(`mistral`, `xai`, `huggingface`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `groq`) have no platform-managed
credentials and need it to run.

x-enumDescriptions.GuardrailImport: Guardrail import adaptor for safety and compliance checks.

guardrail.description:
Selects the check a guardrail applies and carries its settings. `type` picks the check
and the matching sub-object (`pii`, `moderation`, or `aiAgent`) configures it.
Responses echo the active sub-object with `confidenceThreshold` defaulted and also
return the inactive `pii` / `moderation` siblings as empty stubs
(`pii: {entities: [], mask: false}`, `moderation: {categories: []}`) — only the active
type's sub-object is meaningful. Guardrails created before the AI-agent stub was
stripped on write may still return an inert `aiAgent` on `pii` / `moderation` guardrails.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Pick exactly one type. Prefer the deterministic local classifiers (`pii`, then
`moderation`) whenever the brief's intent fits; use `ai_agent` only for custom
judgement that has no `pii.entities` / `moderation.categories` analogue — the full
decision rule is on `type`.

Guardrails never invoke tools. A non-empty `tools` array anywhere under `aiAgent`
(`aiAgent.tools`, `aiAgent.openai.tools`, `aiAgent.litellm._overrides.gemini.tools`,
`aiAgent.litellm._overrides.anthropic.tools`) fails the save with 422
`guardrail_tools_not_allowed`; MCP `prompts` and `resources` are still accepted.

x-enumDescriptions.ai_agent: Evaluate data using an AI model with custom instructions.
x-enumDescriptions.pii: Detect personally identifiable information in data fields.
x-enumDescriptions.moderation: Check content for harmful or inappropriate categories.

type.description:
The type of guardrail to apply. Each type requires its corresponding
sub-configuration object (`aiAgent`, `pii`, or `moderation`).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
The type of guardrail to apply.
Pick exactly one — `pii` / `moderation` / `ai_agent` are mutually exclusive at
the type level (a brief that wants both runs as two guardrails in sequence,
not one).

## How to choose

Apply these rules **in order** and pick the first match.  Do
NOT skip ahead to `ai_agent` just because the brief is in
natural language — `pii` and `moderation` are also expressed
as natural-language briefs.  The decision is about WHAT the
brief asks the guardrail to detect, not how the brief is
worded.

1. **`pii`** — pick this when the brief names ANY personally
   identifiable information, OR when the brief names entity
   categories (SSN, email, phone, credit card, address, name,
   passport, license, account number, etc.) that match
   `pii.entities`.  Examples that route here:
   "detect SSN and credit card numbers", "mask customer
   emails and phone numbers", "scan for PII".

2. **`moderation`** — pick this when the brief asks the
   guardrail to detect harmful, inappropriate, unsafe, or
   policy-violating CONTENT (as opposed to PII data fields)
   AND the intent maps to any value in `moderation.categories`
   (`sexual`, `hate`, `harassment`, `self_harm`, `violence`,
   `illicit`, etc.) — including via close synonyms.  Apply
   the synonym mapping liberally:
   - "explicit", "obscene", "vulgar", "profane",
     "inappropriate language", "swearing", "NSFW" → typically
     maps to `sexual` and/or `harassment`
   - "abusive", "insulting", "bullying", "toxic" → `harassment`
   - "hateful", "discriminatory", "racist", "sexist" → `hate`
   - "threatening", "intimidating" → `harassment_threatening`
     or `violence`
   - "graphic violence", "gore" → `violence_graphic`
   - "suicide", "self-injury" → `self_harm`
   - "drugs", "weapons", "illegal activity" → `illicit`
   Briefs like "screen email body for explicit language",
   "block toxic chat messages", "flag harassment in support
   tickets", "moderate user-generated content for unsafe
   material" all route to `moderation`.  When the brief uses
   a synonym, populate `moderation.categories` with the
   closest enum value(s) — do NOT invent new category
   strings; the enum is fixed.

3. **`ai_agent`** — pick this ONLY when the brief asks for
   judgement that doesn't fit `pii` or `moderation`.  Typical
   triggers: domain-specific compliance checks (HIPAA / SOX
   rule evaluation), business-policy validation (price
   bounds, approval thresholds), data-quality assertions
   (required fields populated, values plausible), or any
   "evaluate against these custom rules" framing where the
   rules are domain-specific and have no `pii.entities` /
   `moderation.categories` analogue.  If you can map the
   brief's intent to a moderation category (even via a
   synonym above), use `moderation` instead — `ai_agent` is
   the catch-all, not the default.

Tie-breaker for borderline cases: prefer the more specific
type (`pii` > `moderation` > `ai_agent`).  `pii` and
`moderation` are local deterministic classifiers with fixed
enums — they're cheaper, faster, and more predictable than
`ai_agent` (which calls a real LLM per record).  Default to
the cheaper path whenever the intent fits.

## Sub-configuration requirements (one per type)

- **ai_agent** requires the `aiAgent` sub-configuration.
- **pii** requires the `pii` sub-configuration with at least
  one entity from `pii.entities`.
- **moderation** requires the `moderation` sub-configuration
  with at least one category from `moderation.categories`.

aiAgent.description:
LLM configuration for an `ai_agent` guardrail — which provider and model evaluate each
record, with instructions, parameter tuning, and output format. Guardrails never invoke
tools, so unlike an AI agent import no block here accepts a `tools` array; MCP `prompts`
and `resources` remain available. Providers come in two families with two configuration
formats:

- **Built-in providers** — each has its own configuration block.
  - **openai**: OpenAI models (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, etc.). Configure via the `openai` object.
  - **gemini**: Google Gemini models via the LiteLLM proxy. Configure via `litellm` with overrides in `litellm._overrides.gemini`.
  - **anthropic**: Anthropic Claude models via the LiteLLM proxy. Configure via `litellm` with overrides in `litellm._overrides.anthropic`.
- **Catalog providers** — `mistral`, `xai`, `huggingface`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `groq`. Added
  as catalog data rather than platform code, they share one generic flat format:
  `model`, `modelOptions`, `instructions`, `output`, and the `prompts` / `resources`
  arrays directly on this object.

A `_connectionId` on the parent import selects bring-your-own-key (BYOK)
credentials. Without one, built-in providers run on platform-managed
credentials; catalog providers have no platform-managed credentials, so they
save without a connection but cannot run until one is attached.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Do not send `tools` on any block. A non-empty array at `tools`, `openai.tools`,
`litellm._overrides.gemini.tools`, or `litellm._overrides.anthropic.tools` fails the
save with 422 `guardrail_tools_not_allowed` naming that path. Responses still echo
`openai.tools: []` on OpenAI guardrails; do not copy it back into a write.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The tools arrays are absent by design — the server rejects a non-empty tools array on every provider block of a guardrail. Do not re-point this schema at the import spec's tool-bearing AI agent config.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server rejects any other value with `provider_not_found`; catalog providers are seeded as data, so new values can appear without a platform release — re-verify before adding one here.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
The provider decides the configuration format, and the server rejects a
mismatch with 422 `invalid_provider_config_format`: `openai` needs the
`openai` block, `gemini` and `anthropic` need the `litellm` block (Gemini- or
Claude-specific settings under `litellm._overrides`), and the catalog
providers (`mistral`, `xai`, `huggingface`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `groq`) need the
generic flat format — `model` and `modelOptions` directly on this object,
never an `openai` or `litellm` block.

Catalog providers are BYOK-only at run time: the guardrail saves without a
`_connectionId`, but its first run fails with 422 `invalid_request` ("No API
key configured for provider …"). Always attach an HTTP connection to the
vendor's API (token auth) when the provider is a catalog provider.

model.description:
Model identifier for a catalog provider (generic flat format) — for example
`grok-4.6`. Built-in providers set the model inside their own block
(`openai.model`, `litellm.model`) instead.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Open string by design — the catalog's model list changes without a spec release, and a BYOK connection passes any model string through to the vendor.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Required for every catalog provider — omitting it or sending an empty string
fails the save with 422 `missing_required_field`.

Without a `_connectionId` on the parent import the model must be one the
catalog lists for the provider: an unknown id fails the save with 422
`model_not_found`, a listed-but-disabled id with 422 `model_disabled`. With a
`_connectionId` (BYOK) any model string saves — the server does not check it
against the catalog or the vendor.

modelOptions.description:
Model tuning for a catalog provider (generic flat format). Which keys, values, and
ranges are accepted is defined per catalog model and validated on save when the
model is a catalog entry.

maxOutputTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens the model may generate.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning depth for models that expose it.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Bounds and the accepted key set differ per catalog model and are enforced by the server's per-model schema; encoding one model's limits here would be wrong for the next.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When the model is a catalog entry, the server validates this object against
that model's schema and fails the save with 422 `invalid_model_options`
naming the key: unknown keys are rejected, `reasoning_effort` must be one of
the enum values where the model accepts it at all (xAI's `grok-4.6` does;
DeepSeek's `deepseek-chat` rejects the key), and numeric bounds apply —
on `grok-4.6`, `temperature` ≤ 2, `topP` ≤ 1, `maxOutputTokens` ≥ 100.

With a `_connectionId` and a model the catalog does not list, the object is
passed through unvalidated — send only options the vendor's API accepts.

mapping.description:
Mapper 1.0 mapping that selects the guardrail's input from the
incoming record. The UI writes a single field entry that maps a
record field to the `text` input (e.g.
`{"fields": [{"extract": "employeeSummary", "generate": "text"}]}`).
Optional — when omitted the whole record is evaluated. The server
serves this field only when populated.

fields.description: Field-level mapping entries; `generate` targets the guardrail input (typically `text`).

generate.description: Target field path to write on the destination record.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Destination field path on the target record. Use the target
system's raw field id — for Salesforce the API name (e.g.
``AccountId``, ``CustomField__c``); for HTTP/REST the JSON
key the endpoint expects; for NetSuite the internal field id
(lowercase, no spaces).

Mapper 1.0 expands two notations into the destination
structure at write time:

- **Dot notation** — ``customer.email`` builds nested
  objects, writing ``{customer: {email: value}}``. Use it
  freely for any depth of nested object on adaptors whose
  payloads are JSON (HTTP, REST, Shopify-style, etc.).
  NetSuite body fields are flat — do not use dot notation
  there.
- **Bracket-star notation** — ``addresses[*].company`` is the
  idiomatic V1 expression for "this scalar belongs to every
  element of the destination array as it is being
  constructed." Two or more ``[*]``-suffixed fields with the
  same array prefix collaborate to populate a single element
  per source record, e.g. pairing
  ``customer.addresses[*].company`` with
  ``customer.addresses[*].city`` produces one address object
  carrying both fields.
- **Numeric bracket notation** — ``addresses[0].company``
  writes to a specific index. It works, but hardcodes the
  slot and is only appropriate when the destination genuinely
  targets a fixed position (rare). Prefer ``[*]`` whenever
  the user describes "an address" / "a line" / "an entry";
  reserve ``[N]`` for "the second address" and similar
  explicit-index intents.

customer.email                  → {"customer": {"email": ...}}
  customer.addresses[*].company   → {"customer": {"addresses": [{"company": ...}]}}
  customer.addresses[*].city      ↑ adds "city" to the same address element

extract.description:
Source expression. Accepts:
- JSONPath starting with `$.` (e.g. `$.customer.firstName`).
- Handlebars template (contains `{{`) for concatenation /
  formatting / conditional logic (e.g.
  `{{record.firstName}} {{record.lastName}}`).
- A literal string (any value not starting with `$.` and not
  containing `{{`) — treated as a hardcoded value.

Omit when using `hardCodedValue`.

hardCodedValue.description: Static value written to `generate` instead of extracting from the source record.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Static value written verbatim. Equivalent to setting ``extract``
to a literal string; choose whichever reads more clearly. Mutually
exclusive with ``extract``.

x-enumDescriptions.number: Numeric data type including integers and decimals.

dataType.description: Data type coercion applied to the mapped value.

discardIfEmpty.description: When true, the field is omitted from the output when the extracted value is empty.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When true, skip this field entirely when ``extract`` / lookup
produces empty / null. Without this flag the destination field
receives null and may overwrite existing data.

immutable.description: When true, the mapped value cannot be overwritten by later mapping steps.

lookupName.description: Name of an entry in the import's `lookups` array used to translate the value.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Name of a lookup defined on ``resource.lookups`` whose result
replaces the extracted value. The looked-up record's
``resultField`` (or full record, depending on lookup shape)

default.description: Fallback value used when the extract yields no value.

extractDateFormat.description: Date format of the source value, used to parse it before conversion.
